source: KICD Environmental Activities, First Published in 2017; Revised 2024 (text layer)
status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

learning_experiences: talk about various things used as bedding at home or school,
role-play how to care for sleeping areas by taking turns cleaning and organising the area,
discuss causes of bedwetting,
mention hygiene practises to observe during bed wetting,
role play on care for bedding,
use digital devices or print media to search for more information on what happens after bed wetting and share with peers,
observe safety precautions and practises when using digital devices to search and watch videos on what happens after bed wetting,
regularly maintain cleanliness and orderliness in the sleeping area at home or school.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is personal hygiene important in your sleeping area?
sub_strands.core_competences: Digital Literacy: learner develops digital skills while observing safety when using digital devices to search and watch videos on what happens after bed wetting.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: learner enhances commitment to making own sleeping area daily.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: learner enhances personal responsibility when caring for bedding.
sub_strands.links: Names of things used as bedding can be used when learning new words in English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: identify locally available things used as bedding
carry out hygiene practises in sleeping areas for a healthy environment
advocate for the importance of observing hygiene in sleeping areas

learning_experiences: discuss about emotions experienced by self and others,
manipulate digital devices to watch video clips or observe pictures of people expressing various emotions,
discuss ways of meeting emotional needs,
role play expressions of emotional needs and how they are met,
match pictures with the emotions expressed,
draw and colour images showing various ways of expressing emotions,
talk about the need for help when role-playing expressions of emotional needs,
sing songs or read stories involving feelings expressed by people,
make posters showing different ways of expressing emotions.
key_inquiry_questions: How do people express their emotions?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy: learner identifies and talks about the need for help when role-playing expressions of emotional needs.
sub_strands.values: Love: learner portrays a caring attitude when comforting others who are hurting.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: learner identifies how to cope with emotions expressed by self and others.
sub_strands.links: Emotional needs in a family draws skills of compassion, empathy, love, and kindness aspects in Religious Activities. Feeling words used in songs and stories involving emotions relates to vocabulary learnt in English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: describe how people express feelings in real-life
describe ways in which emotional needs are met in real-life situations
label emotions expressed by self and others
appreciate the importance of meeting emotional needs in character formation

learning_experiences: share ideas on different food items found in the locality,
use digital devices or print media to search for information on various food groups,
use pictures of common food items or video clips to classify various food items,
use digital devices or print media to search for information on table manners,
role play good table manners when taking meals,
observe good table manners when taking meals,
share reasons why people eat too much or too little food,
use video clips, print media, or age-appropriate case stories to find out what happens when a person eats too much or too little food.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do we have different food items in the locality?
What activities do you engage in while eating?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy: learner develops self-awareness when finding out what happens when a person eats too much or too little food.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner enhances self-drive while observing good table manners when taking meals.
sub_strands.pcis: Health promotion issues: learner advocates for eating the right amount of food to prevent non-communicable diseases.
sub_strands.links: Grouping food items relates to skills of sorting and grouping learnt in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: identify common food items found in the immediate environment
classify food items into three food groups
observe table manners during meals
embrace good eating habits to promote good health

learning_experiences: talk about experiences regarding safety in the community,
discuss how to keep safe in the community,
use pictures, flashcards, or video games to sort and group places into safe and unsafe,
discuss dangerous places in the community,
discuss behaviours that can expose one to danger,
listen to a recorded story or a resource person on how to respond to strangers and other child safety tips,
keenly and actively follow a story from resource persons on different ways of keeping safe in the community,
use digital devices or pictures to identify basic road safety practises,
role play on how to use basic road signs for personal safety (pedestrian crossing, traffic light signs),
take a safety walk around the neighbourhood to identify safe and unsafe places and share findings with peers.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you keep safe in the community?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and Collaboration: learner develops listening skills when following a story keenly and actively from resource persons on different ways of keeping safe in the community.
sub_strands.values: Love: learner enhances a caring attitude when sharing learning resources with peers while working.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: learner develops safety and security awareness when discussing how to keep safe in the community.
sub_strands.links: Basic road safety draws knowledge and concepts from colours in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: identify ways of keeping safe in the community
classify places in the community as safe and unsafe
observe basic road signs for personal safety
acknowledge the importance of keeping safe in the community

learning_experiences: in the community,
practise singing and dancing to songs performed during cultural events in the community,
find out cultural events that promote social well-being and environmental care,
use pictures or video clips to group cultural events that promote environmental care and social well-being in the community,
role play cultural events performed by various communities that promote care for the environment.
key_inquiry_questions: How are cultural events carried out in your community?
sub_strands.core_competences: Citizenship: learner develops active community life skills while finding out cultural events that promote social well-being.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner enhances diligence when accepting assigned roles during cultural events in the community.
sub_strands.pcis: Social cohesion when singing songs in indigenous languages during cultural events.
sub_strands.links: Participation in cultural events relates to skills of singing and dancing in Creative Activities and Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: identify cultural events carried out in the community
recognise cultural events that promote social well-being in the community
classify cultural events that support the community's social well-being and environmental care
embrace cultural events in the community

learning_experiences: share experiences on unfavourable weather conditions in the locality,
use a digital device and print media to search for information on unfavourable weather conditions,
share equitably available learning resources to find out more information on unfavourable weather conditions,
discuss what happens to the environment during unfavourable weather conditions,
read or listen to stories about appropriate responses to unfavourable weather conditions,
talk about appropriate dressing during unfavourable weather conditions,
match unfavourable weather conditions with corresponding safety measures,
practise how to keep safe during unfavourable weather conditions,
gather information from parents or guardians on how to keep safe during unfavourable weather conditions and share with peers.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you keep safe during unfavourable weather conditions?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and Collaboration: learner develops listening and speaking skills while actively engaging in discussions on what happens during unfavourable weather conditions.
sub_strands.values: Social Justice: learner enhances cooperation when equitably shares available learning resources to search for information on unfavourable weather conditions.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: learner makes the right choices on the clothes to wear during unfavourable weather conditions.
sub_strands.links: Reading and listening to stories about appropriate responses to unfavourable weather conditions relates to active listening skills in English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: describe unfavourable weather conditions
explain the dangers of unfavourable weather conditions on people
respond appropriately to unfavourable weather conditions
appreciate the importance of keeping safe during unfavourable weather conditions

learning_experiences: move around the school environment to collect different soil samples,
use the sense of touch to interact with various samples of soil to feel texture,
group different types of soil based on texture,
mount different soil samples on a chart and display the chart in class,
discuss how to care for soil in the environment (manuring, mulching, planting trees),
participate in tree planting activities in the school community,
wash hands after interacting with soil.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we care for soil?
What should be done to protect soil?
sub_strands.core_competences: Collaboration: learner develops decision-making abilities when actively participating in communal tree-planting activities.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism: learner enhances awareness of responsibilities in society when engaging in tree-planting activities.
sub_strands.pcis: Health promotion issues: learner promotes hygiene practises when washing hands after manipulating and interacting with soil.
sub_strands.links: Characteristics of soils relate to modelling concepts in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: list characteristics of different types of soil
carry out basic soil conservation activities in the environment
embrace soil conservation activities in the environment

learning_experiences: think and share on sources of heat used at home,
discuss sources of heat in the environment,
use pictures or video clips to find out various sources of heat in the environment,
discuss uses of heat in the environment and share in class,
discuss basic heat conservation measures,
role-play how to conserve heat in the environment,
share with peers on how to keep safe when dealing with heat from various sources of heat,
reflect on experiences of conserving heat at home and share with others.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is heat important in our daily life?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to Learn: learner reflects on own experiences of conserving heat at home.
sub_strands.values: Respect: learner enhances open-mindedness when appreciating diverse opinions during group discussions on various sources of heat in the environment.
sub_strands.pcis: Socio-economic and Environmental Issues: learner enhances safety and security when sharing with peers on how to keep safe when dealing with heat.
sub_strands.links: Uses of heat relate to concepts about drying clay models in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: list sources of heat in the environment
identify uses of heat in the environment
carry out activities to conserve heat in the environment
appreciate the importance of different sources of heat in daily life

learning_experiences: think and share ideas on sources and uses of water in the environment,
use audio-visual resources or observe pictures to gather information on how water can be contaminated in the environment,
improvise water filters using locally available materials,
clean dirty water through filtration using different materials,
draw and colour an improvised water filter using locally available resources,
discuss how to make water safe for drinking,
discuss ways in which water can be reused,
make posters on ways of conserving water in the environment.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you keep water clean and safe?
sub_strands.core_competences: Creativity and Imagination: learner develops unique and new ideas when using locally available materials to make improvised water filters.
sub_strands.values: Unity: learner enhances team spirit while working collaboratively when making a water filter from locally available materials.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills: learner enhances unity and cooperation instead of competition when making improvised filters from locally available materials.
sub_strands.links: Making improvised filters from locally available materials can be used by learners when learning about sequencing in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: name ways in which water can be contaminated in the environment
carry out activities to make water clean and safe
conserve water at home and school as a scarce resource
value the importance of clean and safe water for healthy living

learning_experiences: listen to a resource person on safety measures observed when handling plants in the environment,
manipulate a digital device to watch video clips or read print media on safety measures to observe when handling plants in the environment,
go on a nature walk to interact with different plants found in the immediate environment,
discuss types of plants (edible, non-edible) found in the locality,
sort and group various plants in the environment as edible/non edible,
draw and colour one type of plant and display it in class,
search from the internet or print media items used to make kitchen gardens,
manipulate digital devices when searching for various forms of kitchen gardens on the internet,
participate in developing a kitchen garden in school using locally available materials as a class project.
key_inquiry_questions: How are plants important in the environment?
sub_strands.core_competences: Digital Literacy: learner manipulates a digital device when searching for various forms of kitchen gardens on the internet.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner embraces hard work when completing assigned tasks in creating a kitchen garden at school.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety: learner enhances safety skills when handling different plants in the environment during a nature walk.
sub_strands.links: Creating a kitchen garden draws knowledge from concepts of measurement (length) in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: identify safety measures to observe when handling plants
classify plants in the environment into edible and non-edible
make a kitchen garden using locally available materials
appreciate plants as sources of food in the locality

learning_experiences: share ideas on types of animals found in the community,
talk about the uses of domestic animals to people,
talk about animals as cart pullers on the roads,
listen to a resource person, or read age appropriate stories on how to care for domestic animals,
role play care for domestic animals,
sing songs about the importance of animals to human beings.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you care for animals at home or school?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to Learn: learner develops the skill of working independently when role-playing care for domestic animals.
sub_strands.values: Love: learner enhances compassion when role playing care for domestic animals.
sub_strands.pcis: Socio-economic and Environmental Issues: learner promotes animal welfare education when advocating for the care of animals including those that provide animal power.
sub_strands.links: Care of animals can be used by learners when learning about creation in Religious Activities.

outcomes.text: explain the importance of domestic animals to human beings
determine ways of caring for domestic animals
engage in activities that care for domestic animals
reflect on the value of domestic animals to human beings

learning_experiences: use pictures, video clips or realia to explore various types of waste materials in the environment,
discuss various ways of using waste to generate income in the immediate environment,
use digital devices or print materials to search for more information on ways of making money from waste,
discuss safety measures to be observed when handling waste materials,
undertake activities that can manage waste materials in the environment using unique and new ideas,
undertake a project that will put waste materials from the environment into appropriate use,
display transparency when accounting for money generated from the project.
key_inquiry_questions: How can waste materials be used to generate income?
sub_strands.core_competences: Creativity and Imagination: learner develops unique and new ideas when undertaking activities that can manage waste materials in the environment.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: learner enhances accountability in displaying transparency when accounting for money generated from the projects.
sub_strands.pcis: Health promotion issues: learner develops habits of safety and hygiene when handling waste materials.
sub_strands.links: Income generation from items made from waste materials is related to concepts of measurement (money) in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: identify waste materials that can be used to generate income
describe ways in which waste materials can generate income
carry out activities to manage waste materials in the environment
value the use of different waste materials to make money in the community
